justifications.durability: The deliverable is a static evidence fragment whose every factual claim is recoverable from the committed fragment text, the run's three gate logs and the two output directories, so a reader can re-check the counts and the ip peaks without the writer. I reproduced the whole read-back independently at DD 4.1.1 (own script, separate from the node's verify_readback.py) and it passed every check, so the record is not dependent on the node's own instrument. Deduction: the claims are bound to artifacts under /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/ids, which the plan states jt60sa-facility-mint §8 will rewrite when the writer moves to run files, so the fragment's numbers are a snapshot rather than a permanent record; and the count-based gate was never falsified (no red), so its discriminating power rests on reading the script rather than on a shown refusal.
justifications.evidence: Every plan done-when check was reproduced by an independent read-back on this allocation: five description IDSs per pulse, pf_active serving exactly 10 coil currents (n_coil=12, FPPC_UP/FPPC_DOWN unserved), magnetics homogeneous_time=0, ip with a time vector as long as its data (46078 samples on 101154, 39612 on 101031), 27 flux loops with data, 17 probes with data, and ip peaks 0.9986 MA (101154) and 0.6984 MA (101031). A positive control on the reader is present: the OP1 store's magnetics.nc reads back with its own 17 probes and angles before the pulse comparison, so the equality result is shown against a live reader rather than an empty one. Deductions: the plan's phrase 'probe axes equal the OP1 store's' is verified beyond the fragment's stated poloidal_angle comparison — I additionally compared toroidal_angle and probe names and both are exact (max delta 0.0, names MP1..., exact) — so the fragment understates rather than overstates the agreement; and the node records the 'was ip-only' pre-state from the plan's §6 rather than from a captured pre-write read, which is plan-sourced and consistent.
justifications.fit: The fragment parses as HTML (html.parser accepts it) and carries 11 element ids, every one beginning with the node id jtpi-write-e101154-e101031 (zero outside the prefix, no duplicates), so sibling fragments composed into one record cannot collide on an anchor. Names and prose describe the two pulses and the writer mechanism; the meta line carries the plan slug, run id and base sha as evidence metadata, the same pattern the sibling machine-map fragment uses. No version tag, plan label, sprint, ticket or issue identifier appears in the body, and no author attribution appears anywhere; the commit subject is conventional with a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The fragment answers §6 honestly and completely: it names both write commands and their exit codes, both output directories, the per-IDS time-dependent leaf counts (pf_active 10, pf_passive 0, wall 0, magnetics 45, tf 1; 68 declared signals left out), the 10 served coil currents, magnetics ip plus 27 flux loops and 17 probes each on its own time vector, the OP1 probe-angle agreement, and the two ip peaks. Magnetics 45 leaves reconciles with the plan's 'ip, 27 flux loops and 17 probes' (1+27+17=45). Deduction: the plan writes no source (jt60sa-facility-mint §8 owns the later rewrite), so an operational node that rewrites E101154 and writes E101031 and records the checks is the whole of the goal, and nothing in the goal is left unaddressed.
justifications.reuse: The node reuses imas-alambic's writer for the write side and imas.DBEntry at DD 4.1.1 on the read side rather than re-deriving either, and it re-reads the writer's own receipt layout (one <ids>.nc per IDS under the shot directory) which the AL backend mandates. It adds only what the goal needs — the fragment and a read-back probe — and changes no library code. Deduction: the read-back probe is bespoke to this node (it was iterated three times per failure_attribution) where a shared read-back helper would serve the sibling write nodes, but that is a pattern observation, not a duplication the node could have avoided within its scope.
